plan.title: AD lesional vs control: DE genes and hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile gives 6 lesional vs 6 control skin RNA-seq samples (raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired, with sample_01 flagged at ~4x below median library depth. The plan follows the grounded procedure from the knowledge service (DESeq2-family workflow implemented in Python via PyDESeq2, since the user requires Python for every script): (1) inspect sample structure with a variance-stabilizing transform, PCA, and a sample-distance heatmap, explicitly reporting sample_01's depth and its position in ordination rather than silently dropping it (R-0008/R-0033); (2) minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size) followed by (3) PyDESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, with an explicit reference level (control) and a named contrast (condition, lesional, control) (R-0026/R-0036); (4) DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, keeping the unshrunken estimate and its SE alongside (R-0001/R-0009/R-0085); (5) Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering, plus a p-value histogram diagnostic (R-0010/R-0083); (6) preranked GSEA (gseapy) against the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) using the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, the enrichment method the knowledge-check confirmed is permitted for this situation (a discrete-list ORA was rejected by the check because the DE gene count is expected to be modest and a short list has no power for ORA); (7) a WikiPathways-human follow-up ORA/GSEA pass on the same ranked list for pathway-resolution triangulation, since WikiPathways is staged as a reference and Hallmark alone is coarse; (8) a final report step assembling MA/dispersion diagnostics, the DE gene table, GSEA leading-edge genes, and full session/version/reproducibility metadata. All scripts are Python per the user's constraint; PyDESeq2 stands in for the R DESeq2/apeglm path the knowledge service names, since only pydeseq2 (not R DESeq2) is combined with a Python-only constraint here, and gseapy stands in for fgsea.
